AfterObtained.rationale: PaelsClaw.cs:32-44 snapshots the deck pile (`.ToList()`, line 34), tests `ModelDb.Enchantment<Goopy>().CanEnchant(item)` (line 37) and calls `CardCmd.Enchant<Goopy>(item, 1m)` (line 39) on every card that passes -- there is NO count limit, so `cardsCount = 3` (line 18) and `CardsVar(3)` (line 26) are description/offer-gate values, not a cap. paels_claw.py:22-24 iterates `list(run.deck)` (the same snapshot), filters on `GoopyEnchantment.can_enchant` and attaches a default-amount Goopy. The amount matches: `CardCmd.Enchant<T>(card, amount)` (CardCmd.cs:518-521) forwards `amount` to `card.EnchantInternal(enchantment, amount)` (CardCmd.cs:532-543), so 1m is the starting Amount, and `Enchantment.__init__`'s default is `amount = 1`. Line 40's NCardEnchantVfx is presentation.

guards.what: N1: Goopy.CanEnchant (Goopy.cs:16-23) = base.CanEnchant AND the Defend tag, vs GoopyEnchantment.can_enchant
guards.rationale: EnchantmentModel.CanEnchant's base contract (no Status/Curse/Quest, no unplayable deck card, one enchantment per card) is mirrored by Enchantment.can_enchant and the Defend-tag clause by `"defend" in card.tags`. NOTE per binding rule 7: this leans on sts2_rl/enchantments.py (lines 51-61 for the base test, 285-287 for the Goopy override), which this record does NOT hash -- a change there goes stale invisibly from here. Also checked: the sim pre-filters with can_enchant before calling attach, and attach itself raises on a failed test, so the two cannot disagree at runtime.

guards.what: N2: Goopy.OnEnchant adds CardKeyword.Exhaust (Goopy.cs:25-28) -- an effect of the ENCHANTMENT, not the relic
guards.rationale: The sim performs it in GoopyEnchantment.attach (enchantments.py:289-291 sets `card.exhausts = True`) and re-applies it per combat in reset (:293-296), so the relic's pickup produces the same card state on both sides. Recorded because the relic is the only ported grant path for Goopy, so a missing OnEnchant here would look like a relic defect.

guards.what: N3: `_enchantmentAmount = 2` (PaelsClaw.cs:20) and `HoverTipFactory.FromEnchantment<Goopy>(2)` (:30) advertise 2 where the code applies 1
guards.rationale: The constant is referenced only by ExtraHoverTips, i.e. the tooltip's sample rendering of the Goopy keyword; the applied amount is the literal 1m at line 39. Presentation-only under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion. Recorded explicitly because PROMPT.md bug class 19 is exactly this trap in reverse -- a port that copies the advertised constant instead of the applied one would set Goopy to 2 and give every Defend +1 Block from its first play. The sim copies the applied value.

guards.what: N4: Goopy's run-level Amount growth. Goopy.AfterCardPlayed (Goopy.cs:29-41) increments base.Amount AND `base.Card.DeckVersion.Enchantment.Amount`, so the growth persists across combats; the sim's GoopyEnchantment grows Amount within a combat only (its own docstring concedes this)
guards.rationale: NOT this unit's divergence, and named here so it is not double-counted: the divergence lives in GoopyEnchantment (sts2_rl/enchantments.py:271-306, not hashed by this record -- binding rule 7), and the enchantment kind is audited on the separate `audit-event` branch, which this worktree does not carry. Pael's Claw's own contract is 'attach Goopy at amount 1 to every eligible deck card', and it does exactly that. Flagged for the enchantment stream rather than verdicted here, since binding rule 3 wants one verdict per mechanism at the site that owns it.

guards.what: N5: Pael.cs:159-162's offer gate (>= 3 Goopy-eligible deck cards) vs paels_claw.py:17's MIN_ELIGIBLE = 3
guards.rationale: The sim's Pael event reads the relic class's own constant (events/pael.py, `if goopy_eligible >= PaelsClaw.MIN_ELIGIBLE`) and counts with the same `GoopyEnchantment.can_enchant` predicate C# counts with. Checked because the gate is the reason `cardsCount = 3` exists at all, and mistaking it for a cap is the obvious way to get this relic wrong.
